smell: Download/fetchToFile/canSkipDownload have no tests at all (only checksum.go and extract.go are covered). The function writes binaries that install.sh and setup.installBinaryToPath then chmod +x and copy into /usr/local/bin under sudo — a wrong code path here lands an attacker-controlled binary in the system PATH. The lack of a symlink-refusal test is also why sec:21dc1103 (no O_NOFOLLOW) survived multiple passes.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — Download writes a file that install.sh later chmod +x's into /usr/local/bin under sudo; lack of any test on this surface let sec:21dc1103 (download-no-nofollow) ship without a regression catch.
fix_summary: Add internal/download/download_test.go: (1) httptest.Server-backed happy-path covering Download → file written at 0o600 with expected bytes; (2) checksum-mismatch retry → second attempt wins; (3) HTTP non-200 returns *HTTPStatusError; (4) ctx-cancel mid-download cleans the partial file (no .partial leftover); (5) symlink at OutputPath path is refused (locks the future O_NOFOLLOW guard from sec:21dc1103); (6) canSkipDownload returns true on existing file with matching checksum, false on size=0, false on checksum mismatch. Use httptest + t.TempDir; no third-party libs.
must_preserve: the existing httputil.New retry behaviour, the bounded retry count, the 0o600 mode on the downloaded file

smell: runlock.Acquire's symlink-refusal guard (Lstat → reject ModeSymlink, then OpenFile with O_NOFOLLOW) is exercised by no test. Acquire runs as root under the deploy/destroy sudo re-exec; a regression that drops the Lstat would let a pre-sudo attacker redirect the root-owned lock file write via a planted symlink. Existing tests (TestAcquireAndRelease, TestConflictMessageContainsHostname, etc.) only cover the happy path and conflict path.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — runlock is acquired before every destructive op (deploy/destroy/cleanup) and runs root-owned under sudo re-exec; a silent regression of the symlink-refusal arm has the same blast radius as the existing logging.go counter-example which IS tested.
fix_summary: Add TestAcquire_RefusesSymlink to runlock_test.go: create dir, symlink .okdctl.lock → /tmp/sentinel, call Acquire(dir, "deploy"), assert *errtypes.ConfigError whose Msg contains "symlink". Skip if os.Geteuid()==0 (root bypasses some symlink restrictions). Mirror cli/logging_test.go:TestOpenLogFileRefusesSymlink as the template — same shape, same skip predicate.
must_preserve: the existing flock-based mutual-exclusion semantics; the test must not race with TestConflictReturnsConfigError

smell: promptForConfirmation is called by every destructive subcommand (deploy, destroy, cleanup, addon uninstall, update-ingress) but has zero direct test coverage. The function has three load-bearing branches that are unverified: (a) no-TTY refusal returning *errtypes.ConfigError, (b) ctx-cancel race vs the inputCh select, (c) isConfirmResponse only accepts y/Y/yes (not 'YES', not 'true'). A regression that loosened isConfirmResponse to strings.HasPrefix('y') would silently swallow ambiguous answers as confirms.
severity_reason: rubric §4 ad-hoc — confirm is the last guard before terraform destroy / oc delete; a regression that auto-confirms without a TTY (e.g. CI pipelines piping into okdctl) would auto-destroy production. The testStdinReader hook is already present in the file, so the test is cheap to write.
fix_summary:
Add tests using the existing testStdinReader hook: (1) testStdinReader=strings.NewReader('y
') → (true, nil); (2) testStdinReader=strings.NewReader('yes
') → (true, nil); (3) testStdinReader=strings.NewReader('n
') → (false, nil); (4) testStdinReader=strings.NewReader('YES
') → (false, nil) (locks case-sensitivity); (5) ctx pre-cancelled → (false, ctx.Err()); (6) testStdinReader=strings.NewReader('') → (false, nil) (EOF treated as not-confirmed). Skip the no-TTY branch since term.IsTerminal can't be stubbed without exposing a hook.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/cli/confirm_test.go (covers sibling but not this function)
Go testing idiom: stdlib testing + table-driven
must_preserve: the no-TTY refusal arm at line 33-37 (the goroutine-leak-bound is documented and intentional)

smell: system.MakeExecutable has no test. It is the canonical 'chmod +x' helper called by setup/release_extract.go (sets +x on extracted oc binary), setup/tools.go (downloaded helper binaries), and setup/artifacts.go — all running as root under the sudo re-exec, all writing to paths that end up in PATH. A bug where mode|0o111 silently degrades to mode (e.g. an off-by-one bit-shift refactor) would land non-executable binaries that fail at runtime mid-deploy.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — used at three setup sites that install root-owned binaries; not on the credential-bearing path so 'major' rather than 'blocker'.
fix_summary: Add to fs_test.go: (1) MakeExecutable on a 0o600 file → mode becomes 0o711 (owner exec preserved through bit-OR); (2) MakeExecutable on a 0o644 file → 0o755; (3) MakeExecutable on 0o600 in a t.TempDir() preserves contents (read body before/after); (4) MakeExecutable on a missing path → wrapped error containing the path. ~30 LOC, table-driven.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (canonical APIs that should not be bypassed must therefore be tested)
must_preserve: the |0o111 semantics — preserves existing read/write bits

smell: WriteAsInvokingUser tests cover the no-sudo and missing-parent-dir branches, but no test exercises the failure mode 'AtomicWrite succeeds, ChownToInvokingUser fails' — in that case the function returns the chown error but leaves the freshly-written file root-owned. That is the operationally important case: deploy crashes mid-flight and the user (no sudo) can't read or rm the kubeconfig the next morning. A test that sets SUDO_UID to an unprivileged uid (65534) on a non-root run, asserts that AtomicWrite succeeded and that the chown error is returned, would lock the failure-shape contract.
severity_reason: rubric §4 ad-hoc — chown failure is the path that strands kubeconfig under root ownership after an aborted deploy; not data-loss but UX-breaking and security-relevant (the operator may then sudo cat the kubeconfig, leaking history).
fix_summary: In elevation_test.go add t.Run('chown-fails-after-write returns the chown error and file persists'): t.Setenv SUDO_UID/SUDO_GID to 65534, call WriteAsInvokingUser on t.TempDir()/x, assert os.Geteuid()!=0 then assert (a) the call returns an error and (b) os.Stat(x) succeeds (file written before chown). Skip when running as root since the chown will succeed.
must_preserve: the current return-on-first-error semantics; do not silently swallow the chown error

smell: cleanupTerraformEnv is well-tested for the happy path and for tfstate preservation (TestCleanupTerraformEnv_PreservesState), but no test covers the partial-failure shape: when SafeRemoveWithLogger fails on terraform.tfstate.backup (e.g. EPERM under non-root tests), the loop continues and the next iteration may also fail — yet the function returns nil because every error is swallowed via discard-assign. A regression where an early failure prevents the .terraform cache directory from being removed would silently leak state across deploys.
fix_summary: Add t.Run('non-removable file logs but does not abort') to infra_test.go: chmod the env-dir parent to 0o500 so .terraform/providers can't be removed but tfvars can; assert (a) err == nil from cleanupTerraformEnv, (b) tfvars was removed, (c) terraform.tfstate still survives. Skip when running as root.

smell: Dnsmasq() has TestDnsmasq_GlobLoopRemovesAllMatches but no test for the cluster-name-driven path: line 153 builds configPath via dns.DnsmasqConfigPath('okd-'+clusterName) and calls os.RemoveAll on it under refuseCriticalPath guard. ClusterName comes from cfg and is validated at config-load, but a hand-edited YAML with an attacker-shaped clusterName (e.g. '../../etc' or 'okd-..%2f..') is the threat the refuseCriticalPath guard exists to catch — and there is no test for that intersection.
fix_summary: Add t.Run('clusterName containing path-traversal segments hits refuseCriticalPath') to services_test.go: monkey-patch dnsmasqConfPattern + dnsmasqBackupPattern (already done by sibling test) and pass clusterName='../../../../etc/okd-x'. Assert that no os.RemoveAll touched anything outside t.TempDir(). Use a t.TempDir() decoy with a sentinel file and check it survives.
must_preserve: the refuseCriticalPath guard; the slices.Contains list of critical paths

smell: Executor.Destroy(UsePlan=true) is exercised by destroy/helpers_test.go:TestDestroyInfrastructure_TFDestroyFails, but the destroyDirect path (UsePlan=false) is dead in tests. okdctl always passes UsePlan=true today (destroy/helpers.go:64), so direct-destroy is scaffolding-shaped: present for future use cases (e.g. emergency destroy without a plan). Lock its argv shape so a regression that flips parallelism handling or target injection is caught.
fix_summary: Either (a) extract the argv-build logic into a buildDestroyArgs helper and table-test it in terraform_test.go, OR (b) add a fake-terraform install (mirroring destroy/helpers_test.go:installFakeTerraform) and call Destroy(UsePlan:false). Option (a) is preferred: smaller blast radius, no PATH manipulation needed.
